title: Human-Controlled AI Release Gate
summary: Convert evaluation, safety, security, privacy, operational, and rollback evidence into an accountable promote, hold, or reject decision.
prerequisites: A versioned release candidate and evaluation report
Named product, risk, and operational owners
A tested rollback or feature-disable path

sections.title: Require evidence from every affected boundary
paragraphs: Bind the decision to exact application, prompt, model, retrieval, tool, policy, data, infrastructure, and grader versions. Require representative and critical-slice evaluation, severe-failure review, security and privacy checks, accessibility evidence, capacity and cost limits, observability, incident ownership, dependency status, migration impact, and a rehearsed rollback.

Keep the approval human and role-based. Automated checks may block a release or assemble evidence, but they must not invent exceptions or approve a consequential change. Record waivers with scope, expiration, compensating controls, and accountable acceptance. Never convert a failed blocking criterion into an undocumented average.

In this synthetic exercise, each boundary has a component identifier and a hash-shaped label. The validator compares strings for exact binding and freshness only. This is not cryptographic verification. A production gate needs controlled artifact storage, authenticated identities, signed or otherwise protected records where appropriate, access controls, and independently auditable verification.

All required dimensions are represented in the manifest, evidence, approval, rollback, reconciliation, decision, and canary files. Missing or explicitly UNKNOWN blocking state produces HOLD. A proven critical failure, candidate mismatch, failed evidence record, threshold breach, or critical canary event produces REJECT.

Priya Shah, Mateo Ruiz, and Lena Okafor are fictional exercise identities for the product, risk, and operations roles. Their records are synthetic data, not real approvals. No file in this exercise authorizes or performs a release.

sections.title: Run the promote, hold, or reject gate
paragraphs: Use staged exposure when consequence or uncertainty warrants it. Define canary population, duration, health signals, safety signals, error budget, cost ceiling, manual kill path, automatic stop conditions, and the evidence required for each expansion. Preserve the previous verified configuration until post-release closeout.

In the worked record, 2 errors divided by 100 events equals 0.02, or 2 percent. That equals, and does not exceed, the 0.02 error budget. The synthetic cost of 0.40 currency units is below the 0.50 ceiling. A single critical event would still stop expansion regardless of these aggregate values.

The filled record is shown before the reusable blank template. Its decision is ELIGIBLE_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW with authorization NONE. That status is neither PROMOTE nor human approval, and it does not mean deployment occurred.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence is an immutable decision record tied to exact artifacts, green blocking thresholds, documented residual risks, named approvers, successful rollback rehearsal, canary observations, and post-release closeout. Verify that deployed hashes and configuration match the human-approved candidate, alerts reach an on-call owner, the disable or rollback control works, and audit evidence excludes secrets and unnecessary user content.

Hold or reject when any blocking threshold fails, required evidence is missing or stale, an owner is absent, a dependency is degraded, rollback is untested, the canary exceeds a stop condition, or actual configuration differs from approval. Recovery means halting expansion, disabling the affected capability or restoring the last verified version, reconciling data and side effects, communicating impact, rerunning the same gate after remediation, and retaining both decisions.

The exercise clock is fixed by manifest.json at 2026-09-13T12:00:00Z. Evidence expiring exactly then is expired because freshness requires expires to be later than as_of. Missing files, malformed JSON, duplicate records, invalid timestamps, non-finite numbers, invalid types, and absent blocking fields produce controlled HOLD output rather than an exception.

Rollback evidence and side-effect reconciliation evidence are separate records. Each has its own identifier, status, immutable exercise link, and executed_in_production field. PASS describes the synthetic rehearsal or review represented by the fixture. It does not claim production execution.
sections.callout: Automation can enforce a gate; accountability for accepting residual risk remains human.

sections.title: Runnable standard-library validator
paragraphs: Save this file as validator.py. It uses only Python 3 standard-library modules, reads local JSON, and writes only its result to standard output. It does not deploy, approve, authorize, roll back, reconcile, authenticate identities, or cryptographically verify hashes.

All input shapes, types, finite numeric ranges, timestamps, duplicate-sensitive lists, and required fields are checked before arithmetic or set operations. Missing files and malformed JSON return HOLD. REJECT takes precedence when a proven critical condition is present. Otherwise, invalid or unknown blocking state returns HOLD. Only a fully valid baseline returns ELIGIBLE_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW with authorization NONE.

code.label: validator.py

sections.title: Defective inputs and fail-closed cases
paragraphs: The unittest file creates temporary defective fixtures from the complete baseline, so no patch commands or incomplete fixture directories are required. It tests expiry equality, missing and failed evidence, stale evidence, candidate and component mismatches, malformed numeric and boolean values, non-finite numbers, zero events, negative values, errors exceeding events, duplicate records and roles, empty names, invalid manual kill and duration, missing files, malformed JSON, invalid timestamps, critical-event precedence, and the changed candidate.
Every expected result is synthetic and deterministically derived from the supplied validator and fixture values. No execution is claimed in this resource.

sections.title: Complete offline validation tests
paragraphs: Save this as test_validator.py beside validator.py. Run it from the directory that contains validator.py and fixtures. The test suite uses temporary local directories and performs no network access or remote writes.

sections.title: Offline commands and synthetic expected output
paragraphs: Run these commands from the directory containing validator.py, test_validator.py, and fixtures. They require Python 3 and no third-party packages. They perform local reads and temporary test-file writes only. They do not download, call a provider, deploy, roll back, reconcile, or write remotely.

The outputs are expected outputs derived from the supplied code. They are not claims of actual execution. unittest timing and individual test-order lines can vary by Python version, so the stable asserted summary is 34 tests and OK.

python3 validator.py fixtures/baseline

EXPECTED SYNTHETIC OUTPUT
{"authorization": "NONE", "deployment": "NOT_PERFORMED", "reasons": [], "status": "ELIGIBLE_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW"}

Interpretation: passing tests establish only that this local validator behaves as asserted on these fixtures. They do not establish authorization, deployment, cryptographic integrity, production safety, or provider behavior.

sections.title: Changed-input learner task
paragraphs: Before reading the solution, create a separate complete directory named fixtures/changed. Change the model identifier and hash to model-5 and sha256:model-new. Change candidate_id to candidate-2026-09-13-b in manifest.json, evidence.json, rollback.json, reconciliation.json, canary.json, and decision.json, but deliberately leave approvals.json bound to candidate-2026-09-13-a. Set canary critical_events to 1 while keeping events at 100, errors at 2, and cost at 0.40. Use the same validator without editing it.

Predict the status and exact sorted reasons. Explain why approval for candidate a cannot transfer to candidate b, why 2 divided by 100 does not exceed a 0.02 budget, why one critical event still stops expansion, and what new candidate-bound evaluation, approval, rollback, reconciliation, canary, and decision evidence humans would need before reconsideration.

sections.title: Changed-input solution, tests, and feedback
paragraphs: Run python3 validator.py fixtures/changed. The deterministic synthetic expected result is REJECT with exactly approvals-candidate-mismatch and critical-canary-event-stop. The supplied unittest test_changed_candidate_solution applies the same changes to a temporary complete fixture and asserts those exact sorted reasons with authorization NONE.

Approval for candidate a cannot transfer because candidate b includes a changed model binding and therefore represents a different reviewed object. The arithmetic 2 / 100 = 0.02 equals the budget, so the error average does not reject. The one critical event independently rejects and stops expansion. Before reconsideration, investigate and remediate the critical event, rerun candidate-b evaluation and canary evidence, confirm rollback and reconciliation for candidate b, obtain fresh authenticated role decisions bound to candidate b, and create a new retained decision record.

Actionable feedback: if you got HOLD, inspect whether you treated the two proven failures merely as unknowns. If you got eligible, verify the approvals candidate_id and critical_events. If you got PROMOTE, remove that conclusion because this validator cannot promote or authorize. If you got extra mismatch reasons, check that candidate_id was changed in every requested file except approvals.json and that the model evidence exactly matches the changed manifest.

sections.title: Provider-neutral transfer and exercise limits
paragraphs: The gate applies to a system boundary, not a brand. The model component may be hosted, self-managed, or from an optional family such as Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, or Z.ai. A family name does not establish context limits, safety behavior, tool support, licensing, latency, cost, or deployment controls. Record deployment-specific identifiers, configurations, capabilities, evaluations, and owners instead of assuming vendor behavior.

The process transfers beyond any three vendors because it depends on versioned evidence, role-based human decisions, staged exposure, stop criteria, rollback, reconciliation, and closeout. Provider-specific adapters may collect configuration or metrics, but they cannot approve a consequential change or silently waive missing evidence. Exercise correctness is independently testable without a paid account.

This exercise does not implement cryptographic verification, authenticated identities, signed approvals, tamper-resistant storage, production observability, real traffic, real user data, provider-specific safety guarantees, or side-effect execution. Those capabilities are UNKNOWN here and must block a real release until separately evidenced. Hash-shaped fixture strings prove only exact string equality inside the exercise.

The gate framing follows the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and its Generative AI Profile. The linked OpenAI and Google documentation provide provider-specific safety evaluation guidance, but this exercise does not infer or invent behavior for any provider.

sections.title: Reusable decision template
